walkthroughs.body_html:
Clinical Psychology — a core area of A-Level Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Clinical Psychology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Clinical Psychology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Top-down offender profiling was developed by:
options: Canter
FBI
Lombroso
Eysenck

mcqs.q: Differential association theory was proposed by:
options: Sutherland
Eysenck
Bandura
Lombroso

mcqs.q: What did Bowlby mean by monotropy?
options: Cries continuously and cannot be comforted.
One primary attachment figure (usually the mother) is qualitatively different and most important.
A child can only ever form one attachment.
All attachments are equally important.

mcqs.q: Which part of the psyche operates on the reality principle?
options: The id (pleasure principle).
All attachments are equally important.
The ego.
The superego (moral principle).

mcqs.q: How does a securely attached infant respond to reunion with the caregiver?
options: The id (pleasure principle).
Shows no distress and ignores the caregiver.
Cries continuously and cannot be comforted.
Seeks comfort and is easily soothed, then returns to play.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Differential association”?
options: Criminals score high on extraversion, neuroticism and psychoticism (E, N, P); inherited nervous system underactivity.
Sutherland (1939): criminal behaviour learned from associates whose pro-crime attitudes outweigh anti-crime ones.
Imprisonment aims to deter, rehabilitate, incapacitate and protect; UK recidivism around 48% within one year.
FBI approach (Ressler 1986): classify crime scene as organised or disorganised to infer offender characteristics.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Bottom-up profiling”?
options: Imprisonment aims to deter, rehabilitate, incapacitate and protect; UK recidivism around 48% within one year.
Canter's UK approach: statistical analysis of crime scene data to derive profiles; investigative psychology.
Lombroso's (1876) outdated theory that criminals are evolutionary throwbacks identifiable by physical features.
Sutherland (1939): criminal behaviour learned from associates whose pro-crime attitudes outweigh anti-crime ones.
